spine_tilt_address.human_explanation: This measures your spine tilt *away* from the target at setup. Your score was low because your spine was too 'level' (vertical). Pros tilt their spine *behind* the ball to create the 'Reverse K' position, which is essential for the driver.
spine_tilt_address.why_it_matters: This is a major 'root cause' for a slice. Tilting your spine *away* from the target is the secret to hitting 'up' on the ball (a positive 'Angle of Attack'). A 'level' setup forces you to hit 'down' on the ball, which causes slices and a massive loss of distance.

drills.name: The 'Hip Bump' Drill
drills.instructions: Set up normally with the ball off your lead instep. Now, *without moving your head*, just 'bump' your lead hip 1-2 inches toward the target. You will feel your spine automatically tilt back. This is the 'Reverse K' position. Hit 50% shots feeling this.

drills.name: The 'Club on Chest' Drill
drills.instructions: Hold your driver vertically against your chest (clubhead up). Get in your posture. Now, tilt your *entire* upper body (and the club) away from the target until the clubhead is over your trail (back) foot. This is the correct feel.

hip_sway_impact.human_explanation: This measures your 'weight shift.' Your score was low because your hips 'hung back' (stayed behind the ball). Pros shift their hips *aggressively forward* (4-5 inches) toward the target to lead the downswing.
hip_sway_impact.why_it_matters: The 'hip bump' toward the target is the *engine* of your downswing. It creates space, shallows the club, and transfers all your weight *through* the ball for maximum power. 'Hanging back' forces you to 'cast' the club with just your arms, leading to a weak, 'scooped' shot.

drills.name: The 'Step-Through' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit an easy 70% shot. As you swing *through* impact, let your *back* foot come off the ground and take a full step *forward* (like a baseball pitcher). It's impossible to do this if your weight is stuck on your back foot.

drills.name: The 'Bump the Bag' Drill
drills.instructions: Place your golf bag on the *outside* of your *lead* foot. As you start your downswing, your very first move should be to 'bump' the bag with your lead hip. This teaches you the 'lateral shift' *before* you rotate.

head_position_impact.human_explanation: This measures your head's position relative to the ball at impact. Your score was low because your head 'lunged' *forward* (in front of the ball). Pros keep their head *behind* the ball to maintain their spine tilt.
head_position_impact.why_it_matters: Keeping your head 'behind the ball' is the key to creating an 'upward' Angle of Attack and maintaining your power. When your head lunges forward, it forces your shoulders to open early and your club to swing 'over-the-top,' which is a primary cause of a steep, slicing shot.

drills.name: The 'Back Foot Ball' Drill
drills.instructions: Place another ball (or headcover) on the ground *inside* your *trail* (back) foot. As you swing, your *only* focus is to keep your head 'over' that second ball. This feel will stop you from lunging forward.

drills.name: The 'Alignment Stick' Drill
drills.instructions: Have a friend hold an alignment stick or club vertically, just touching the *lead* (front) side of your head at address. Your goal is to make a full swing *without* hitting the stick. This gives you instant feedback on any forward lunge.

spine_tilt_impact.human_explanation: This measures your spine tilt *away* from the target at the moment of impact. Your score was low because your upper body 'lunged' forward, causing your spine to become too vertical. Pros *increase* this tilt to create a powerful, upward launch.
spine_tilt_impact.why_it_matters: This is the 'launch' position. Increasing your spine tilt at impact is the ultimate 'power move'—it's the *only* way to hit 'up' on the ball (positive AOA) while your weight is correctly shifted forward. Losing this tilt causes a steep 'over-the-top' swing, slices, and a huge loss of power.

drills.name: The 'Head Back' Drill
drills.instructions: Your spine tilt is a *result* of your head position. Your #1 fix is to practice the 'Back Foot Ball' drill. Focus *only* on keeping your head behind the ball through impact. Your spine will naturally stay tilted.

drills.name: The 'Lead Hip Up' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a pro-level feel. As you swing through, feel your *lead* (front) hip working 'up and back' (away from the target line). This 'pulls' your lead shoulder up, *drops* your trail shoulder, and *automatically* increases your spine tilt.

arm_extension_finish.human_explanation: This measures how 'wide' you finish. Your score was low because your lead arm was 'bent' (a 'chicken wing'). Pros finish 'high and wide' with both arms extended, showing a full release of energy.
arm_extension_finish.why_it_matters: A 'chicken wing' finish is a 'symptom' of a flaw that happened *before* impact. It's your body's way of saving a bad swing! It's almost always caused by an 'over-the-top' path or 'hip thrust' (Early Extension), which forces you to pull your arms in to make contact.

drills.name: The 'Throw the Club' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit a 50% shot. After impact, your *only* thought is to feel like you are 'throwing' the clubhead as far *down the target line* as possible. This forces your arms to extend.

drills.name: The 'One-Arm Only' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit very small, 30% speed shots using *only* your lead arm. It is *impossible* to hit the ball this way without rotating your body and keeping your lead arm extended. This is a pro-level drill for building a perfect release.

hip_sway_backswing.human_explanation: This measures how much your hips move 'side-to-side' in your backswing. Your score was low because your hips 'swayed' *away* from the target. Pros 'rotate' their hips around a stable center.
hip_sway_backswing.why_it_matters: A 'hip sway' is a major power leak. It's the root cause of 'hanging back' on your downswing, which robs you of power and makes it impossible to be consistent. A proper 'rotation' builds up power like a coiling spring, ready to unleash.

drills.name: The 'Wall' Drill (or Golf Bag)
drills.instructions: Set up with your *trail* (back) hip just touching a wall or your golf bag. Your goal is to make a full backswing and feel your hip *rotate*, but *without* 'pushing' hard into the wall. This is the ultimate feedback for stopping a sway.

drills.name: The 'One-Leg' Drill
drills.instructions: Set up, then lift your *lead* (front) foot just off the ground. Now, try to make a slow, half-backswing. If you 'sway', you will lose your balance immediately. This forces you to 'rotate' around your trail leg.

head_movement_lateral.human_explanation: This measures how much your head moves 'side-to-side' in your backswing. Your score was low because your head 'swayed' *away* from the target. Pros keep their head very centered, like an 'anchor' for their body to rotate around.
head_movement_lateral.why_it_matters: A 'swaying' head is a classic *symptom* of a 'hip sway.' When your head moves off the ball, your entire swing center moves, forcing you to 'hang back' on the downswing just to make contact. This kills power and consistency.

drills.name: The 'Nose on the Wall' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a simple feedback drill. Set up in your posture at home with your nose *just* touching a wall. Make slow backswings. You will instantly feel if your head 'sways' (pushes into the wall) or 'lifts'.

drills.name: The 'Root Cause' Fix
drills.instructions: Your head sway is caused by your 'hip sway.' Your #1 fix is to practice the 'Wall Drill' for your hips. When you learn to *rotate* your hips instead of 'swaying' them, your head will automatically stay centered.

shoulder_turn_top.human_explanation: This measures the 'tilt' of your shoulder turn. Your score was low because your shoulders are 'spinning' too 'flat' (level with the ground). Pros create power by making a 'tilted' turn, with their lead shoulder working 'down and under' their chin.
shoulder_turn_top.why_it_matters: A 'flat' shoulder turn is a massive power leak. It's a 'root cause' for an 'arms-only' swing that forces you to 'sway' off the ball and leads to an 'over-the-top' path. A deep, 'tilted' turn 'coils' your upper body like a spring, loading up maximum power.

drills.name: The 'Club Across Shoulders' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a club across your shoulders and get into your address posture. Now, make your backswing turn. Your goal is to tilt your shoulders so the butt-end of the club points *down* at the golf ball. If it points 'out' (level to the ground), your turn is too flat.

drills.name: The 'Lead Shoulder to Back Knee' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. As you make your backswing, your *only* thought should be 'get your lead shoulder over your trail (back) knee.' This feel forces your lead shoulder to work *down* and *across*, creating the perfect pro-level tilt.

shaft_lean_address.human_explanation: This measures your shaft lean at setup. Your score was low because your hands were too far *in front* of the clubhead ('forward lean'). For a driver, pros set up with their hands 'neutral' or even slightly *behind* the ball.
shaft_lean_address.why_it_matters: Setting up with 'forward lean' (like an iron) is a 'root cause' that *forces* you to hit 'down' on the ball. This creates a steep, slicing path and a low `angle_of_attack`. A 'neutral' or 'backward' lean is the key to 'sweeping' the ball on an *upward* path for maximum distance.

drills.name: The 'Lead Arm-Shaft Line' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a simple setup key. At address, your *lead* (front) arm and the club shaft should form one, continuous straight line, from your lead shoulder down to the clubhead. Your hands should not be 'pushing' the club forward.

drills.name: The 'Butt-End to Zipper' Drill
drills.instructions: Get in your driver setup. The butt-end of your club should be pointing at your zipper or belt buckle. If it's pointing at your *lead* (front) leg, your hands are too far forward.

lag_loss_downswing.human_explanation: This measures 'lag,' which is the 'snap' in your swing. Your score was low because you are 'casting' or 'throwing' the club from the top. Pros 'store' this angle (like a whip) and release it at the ball.
lag_loss_downswing.why_it_matters: This is the #1 power leak in golf. 'Casting' wastes all your stored energy *before* you get to the ball, leading to low clubhead speed. It also forces you to hit 'down' on the driver, causing pop-ups or weak, 'scoopy' shots.

drills.name: The 'Pump' Drill
drills.instructions: Make your backswing. On the way down, 'pump' the club twice: swing down to where your hands are at your hip (feeling the 'lag' angle), go back to the top, then 'pump' again. On the third 'pump', swing all the way through.

drills.name: The 'Trail Hand Off' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit 50% shots with *only* your lead hand (e.g., left hand) on the club. It is *impossible* to 'cast' the club this way. This will force you to use your *body* to pull the club through and will build the 'lag' feeling.

angle_of_attack.human_explanation: This metric, 'Angle of Attack' (AOA), measures if you are hitting 'up' or 'down' on the ball. Your score was low because you hit 'down' (a negative number), which is the #1 distance-killer for most amateurs.
angle_of_attack.why_it_matters: To get the most distance, you MUST hit 'up' on the driver (a positive AOA). This is the 'holy grail' of driving because it launches the ball **high** while keeping backspin **low**. Hitting 'down' does the opposite, creating low, spinny shots that 'balloon' and go nowhere.

drills.name: The Simple Tee Fix
drills.instructions: This is the easiest fix. Tee the ball higher so that the *entire* golf ball is above the top edge of your driver. This naturally forces your body to swing 'up' to make contact.

drills.name: The Headcover Drill
drills.instructions: Place your empty driver headcover on the ground about one foot in front of your teed-up ball, directly on your target line. Your only goal is to make a full swing and miss the headcover. If you hit 'down' on the ball, you will hit the headcover.

club_path.human_explanation: This is the 'king' of all swing metrics. It measures the horizontal direction your club is moving at impact. A neutral path (0.0°) hits straight shots.
club_path.why_it_matters: This metric directly controls the starting direction and curve of your ball. An 'out-to-in' path (negative number) is the #1 cause of a SLICE. An 'in-to-out' path (positive number) is the #1 cause of a HOOK. Getting this number near zero is the secret to consistency.

drills.name: The Gate Drill (Fix for a Slice)
drills.instructions: Place two headcovers on the ground, forming a 'gate' just wide enough for your clubhead to pass through. This forces you to swing 'in-to-out' and neutralizes your 'out-to-in' slice path.

drills.name: The 'Miss the Box' Drill (Fix for a Slice)
drills.instructions: Place an empty golf ball box on the ground just outside your ball, on your target line. Your goal is to swing 'from the inside' and miss the box. This will cure your 'over-the-top' slice.

drills.name: The 'Hands-In' Drill (Fix for a Hook)
drills.instructions: Set up normally. Now, try to feel like your hands are swinging 'in' (closer to your body) *through* impact. This will stop you from 'pushing' the club so far 'out-to-in' and will neutralize your hook.

drills.name: The 'Back to the Target' Drill (Fix for a Hook)
drills.instructions: After you hit the ball, focus on feeling like the *back* of your lead hand (e.g., left hand for a righty) faces the target for as long as possible. This will stop you from 'flipping' your hands and curing that big hook.

spine_bend_address.human_explanation: This measures your forward bend from your hips. Your score was low because you are 'slumping' your shoulders to reach the ball (a 'C-Posture'). A good swing starts with an athletic 'hip hinge' and a relatively straight back.
spine_bend_address.why_it_matters: A 'C-Posture' at address is a 'swing killer.' It physically blocks your shoulders from rotating. This lack of rotation is a root cause for many flaws, as it forces your arms to 'lift,' leading directly to an 'over-the-top' swing path and a loss of power.

drills.name: The 'Wall Hinge' Drill
drills.instructions: Stand straight, club across your shoulders. Now, push your hips *straight back* (like closing a car door with your butt) until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings. That's the 'hinge.' Now, just soften your knees. This is the perfect address posture.

drills.name: The 'Club on Back' Drill
drills.instructions: Hold a club vertically along your spine, making sure it touches your tailbone AND the back of your head. Now, perform the 'Hip Hinge' drill. If the club stays in contact with both points, your back is straight. If it loses contact, you are 'slumping'.

shaft_angle_top.human_explanation: This measures where your club is 'pointing' at the top of your swing. The 'pro' ideal is 'on plane' (0.0°), where the club is parallel to your target line.
shaft_angle_top.why_it_matters: This position sets up your *entire* downswing. If you are 'across the line' (pointing right), you are forced to re-route the club, often leading to an 'over-the-top' slice. If you are 'laid off' (pointing left), your arms can get 'stuck' behind you, leading to hooks or pushes.

drills.name: The 'Armpit' Drill (Fix for Across the Line)
drills.instructions: Place an empty glove or small headcover under your trail (back) armpit. Make a backswing—your goal is to keep it there all the way to the top. This keeps your arm connected to your body and stops you from 'running on' across the line.

drills.name: The 'Stop at the Top' Drill (Fix for Across the Line)
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. Make a slow backswing, but *stop* when your hands reach shoulder height. Feel the balance. Now, finish your shoulder turn *without* letting your arms lift further. This teaches you to separate your 'turn' from your 'arm lift'.

drills.name: The 'Left Hand Logo' Drill (Fix for Laid Off)
drills.instructions: At the top of your swing, look at the logo on your lead hand's glove (e.g., left hand for a righty). That logo should be pointing at the sky or at a 45-degree angle. If it's pointing at the target, you are 'laid off'.

early_extension.human_explanation: This metric checks if your hips are thrusting *toward* the ball on your downswing. Your score was low because your hips moved forward, causing you to 'stand up' out of your posture. This is a very common flaw called 'Early Extension'.
early_extension.why_it_matters: This is a 'root cause' flaw. When your hips thrust forward, they block the path for your arms. This 'blocks' your swing, forcing your arms to get stuck behind you (causing hooks) or re-route 'over-the-top' (causing slices). Pros keep their hips *back* to create space for their arms to accelerate.

drills.name: The 'Golf Bag' Drill
drills.instructions: Set up with your tailbone just *barely* touching your golf bag. Your goal is to make a full swing where your hips *rotate*, but do not 'push' the bag over. You should feel your trail hip stay back.

drills.name: The 'Chair' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a chair just behind your trail hip. As you start your downswing, feel like you are trying to 'sit back' into the chair. This is the 'pro' move of creating space by keeping your posture.

takeaway_path.human_explanation: This measures the path of your club in the first few feet of your swing. Your score was low because you 'pulled' the club 'inside' (behind your body). The 'pro' move is a 'one-piece' takeaway, where the clubhead stays 'out' in front of you.
takeaway_path.why_it_matters: This is a major 'root cause' flaw. Pulling the club 'inside' right away gets it 'stuck' behind your body. From there, your brain's only option is to throw the club 'over-the-top' on the downswing to get it back to the ball. This is a primary source of a slice.

drills.name: The 'Two-Ball' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a second golf ball on the ground about 6 inches behind your teed-up ball, but 1 inch *inside* your target line. Your goal is to push the clubhead *straight back* and hit the second ball. This will cure your 'inside' takeaway.

drills.name: The 'One-Piece' Feel
drills.instructions: Set up normally. Now, try to feel like your hands, arms, and chest all move *together* as one 'triangle' for the first 2 feet. Don't let your wrists 'roll' the club inside.

drills.name: The 'Miss the Headcover' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a headcover on the ground just *inside* your clubhead at address. Your goal is to start your swing and *miss* the headcover. This forces you to take the club away 'wider' and stops you from pulling it inside.

head_movement_vertical.human_explanation: This measures how much your head moves 'up' or 'down' during your swing. A stable head acts as an anchor for your body to rotate around.
head_movement_vertical.why_it_matters: If your head 'dips' too much in the backswing, it forces your body to 'stand up' just to make contact, leading to 'Early Extension' and thin shots. If your head 'lifts' at impact, that's a sure sign your hips are thrusting toward the ball (Early Extension), which is a major source of slices and hooks.

drills.name: The 'Head Against a Wall' Drill
drills.instructions: In your home, get into your golf posture with the *top* of your head lightly touching a wall. Make slow backswings. If you 'dip', you'll feel your head press *harder* into the wall. If you 'lift', it will come off the wall. This gives you perfect feedback.

drills.name: The 'Shaft Across Shoulders' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a club across your shoulders and get into your posture. Now, make your backswing 'turn'. The butt of the club should point *down* at the ground, well behind the ball. If you 'dip', the shaft will point more 'level' with the ground.

drills.name: The 'Golf Bag' Drill (Fix for Lifting)
drills.instructions: Your 'lifting' problem is a *symptom* of 'Early Extension'. Set up with your tailbone *barely* touching your golf bag. Your goal is to make a full swing where your hips *rotate*, but do not 'push' the bag over. This keeps your posture and stops your head from lifting.

shaft_shallowing.human_explanation: This is a pro-level metric. It measures if you 'shallow' the club (flatten it) on the downswing. Your score was low because you 'steepened' the club, which is a primary cause of an 'over-the-top' slice.
shaft_shallowing.why_it_matters: Shallowing the club is the secret to attacking 'from the inside.' It creates space, neutralizes a slice, and is a root cause of effortless power. Steepening the club forces you to chop down on the ball, leading to weak slices or pulls.

drills.name: The 'Trail Elbow' Drill
drills.instructions: As you start your downswing, feel your trail (back) elbow drive *down* towards your trail hip. This will automatically 'drop' the club into the 'shallow' slot behind you. Amateurs let their trail elbow fly 'out', which causes the steepening.

drills.name: The 'Face-Down' Drill
drills.instructions: Make a slow downswing and *stop* when the shaft is parallel to the ground. Look at the clubface. It should be pointing slightly *down* at the ground. This is only possible if you are shallowing the club and rotating your body correctly.

shoulder_plane_top.human_explanation: This measures the 'tilt' of your shoulder turn. Your score was low because your shoulders are 'spinning' too 'flat' (level with the ground). Pros turn on a steep 'tilt,' with their lead shoulder working 'down and under' their chin.
shoulder_plane_top.why_it_matters: A 'flat' shoulder turn is a massive power leak. It's a 'root cause' for an 'arms-only' swing that forces you to 'sway' off the ball and leads to an 'over-the-top' path. A deep, 'tilted' turn 'coils' your upper body like a spring, loading up maximum power.

drills.name: The 'Club Across Shoulders' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a club across your shoulders and get into your address posture. Now, make your backswing turn. Your goal is to tilt your shoulders so the butt-end of the club points *down* at the golf ball. If it points 'out' (level to the ground), your turn is too flat.

drills.name: The 'Lead Shoulder Down' Feel
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. As you make your backswing, your *only* thought should be 'lead shoulder to the back foot's big toe.' This feel forces your lead shoulder to work *down* and *across*, creating the perfect pro-level tilt.

drills.name: The 'Trail Shoulder Up' Drill
drills.instructions: From your DTL view, feel your *trail* (back) shoulder rotate 'up and back' (like you're looking under your chin) instead of just 'around'. This will help create the space and tilt you need.

hip_depth_top.human_explanation: This measures how much 'space' you create by moving your hips *back* and *away* from the ball in your backswing. Your score was low because your hips stayed in place or even moved *toward* the ball.
hip_depth_top.why_it_matters: This is a massive 'root cause' flaw. Pros create 3-4 inches of 'hip depth' (space) to make room for their arms. Amateurs who 'lose' this space have nowhere to go, which *forces* their hips to thrust *forward* on the downswing (Early Extension), leading to slices and hooks.

drills.name: The 'Back Pocket' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. As you start your backswing, feel your *trail* (back) hip pocket move 'up and back' as if you're reaching for the wall behind you. This is the feeling of creating depth.

drills.name: The 'Backside Wall' Drill
drills.instructions: Set up with your tailbone just *barely* touching a wall or your golf bag (just like our 'Early Extension' drill). Now, as you make your backswing, feel your *trail* (back) hip/glute push *back* into the wall. This is a perfect rep.

trail_leg_flex_top.human_explanation: This measures the flex in your trail (back) leg at the top. Your score was low because your leg is 'locking' (straightening) too much. Pros maintain their flex, using their trail leg as a 'stable post' to rotate against.
trail_leg_flex_top.why_it_matters: When your trail leg 'locks' straight, it's impossible for your hips to turn correctly. This is a major 'root cause' that *forces* your hips to 'sway' off the ball, which leads to a 'reverse pivot' (leaning toward the target) and a massive loss of power and consistency.

drills.name: The 'Pressure on Instep' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. As you make your backswing, your *only* thought should be to keep pressure on the *instep* (the inside) of your trail foot. If you 'lock' your leg, you will feel the pressure roll to the *outside* of your foot.

drills.name: The 'One-Knee' Drill
drills.instructions: Take your address. Now, slightly 'kick in' your trail knee (toward your lead knee). Your goal is to make a backswing and *keep* that inward-pointing knee flex. This will feel like a powerful 'brace' and stop you from locking your leg.

backswing_width.human_explanation: This measures how 'wide' your swing arc is. Your score was low because your arms are 'collapsing' (getting too close to your head) at the top. Pros create power by 'pushing' their hands *away* from their body.
backswing_width.why_it_matters: Width is power. A 'narrow' swing with 'collapsed' arms has a small arc and no speed. It's a major 'root cause' that forces you to 'cast' the club from the top, leading to an 'over-the-top' path and a huge loss of distance.

drills.name: The 'Straight Arm' Takeaway
drills.instructions: For the first part of your backswing (until the club is parallel to the ground), feel like your *lead* (front) arm stays perfectly straight and 'pushes' the club away. This sets the width for the entire swing.

drills.name: The 'Ball Squeeze' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a small, partially-deflated beach ball or pillow between your forearms. Make 50% swings. Your goal is to keep the ball *squeezed* between your arms all the way to the top. If your arms 'collapse', you'll drop the ball.

wrist_set_top.human_explanation: This measures your lead wrist position at the top. Your score was low because your wrist is 'cupped' (bent backwards). Pros are 'flat' or 'bowed' (bent forwards), which is a key power and control move.
wrist_set_top.why_it_matters: This is a primary 'root cause' of a slice. A 'cupped' wrist *opens* the clubface at the top. From there, your body is forced to swing 'over-the-top' to try and save the shot. A 'flat' or 'bowed' wrist squares the clubface *early*, so you can shallow the club and rotate hard without worrying about a slice.

drills.name: The 'Motorcycle' Drill
drills.instructions: As you get to the top of your swing, feel like you are revving a motorcycle with your lead hand. This 'bowing' motion will flatten your wrist and square the clubface. Hit 50% shots just feeling this move.

drills.name: The 'Hanger' Drill
drills.instructions: Get a plastic clothes hanger and clip it to your grip (hook facing down the shaft). Make a backswing. If your wrist is 'cupped', the hook of the hanger will *come off* your lead forearm. If you are 'flat', it will *stay pressed against* your forearm. This is perfect feedback.

spine_tilt_address.human_explanation: This measures your spine tilt at setup. Your score was low because your spine was 'level' or 'forward.' For a fairway wood/hybrid, pros use a *slight* tilt *away* from the target to promote a 'sweeping' motion.
spine_tilt_address.why_it_matters: This setup flaw is a 'root cause' for 'fat' shots. A 'level' or 'forward' spine tilt forces you to hit 'down' on the ball like an iron. A slight *away* tilt is the key to 'sweeping' the ball off the grass for a high, powerful launch.

drills.name: The 'Ball Position' Fix
drills.instructions: This is a simple setup key. Make sure the ball is positioned just *inside* your *lead* (front) heel. Then, simply let your hands hang naturally. This will create the perfect, slight spine tilt.

drills.name: The 'Hip Bump' Drill
drills.instructions: Set up normally. Now, *without moving your head*, just 'bump' your lead hip 1 inch toward the target. You will feel your spine automatically tilt back slightly. This is the perfect setup to 'sweep' the ball.

hip_sway_impact.human_explanation: This measures your 'weight shift.' Your score was low because your hips 'hung back' (stayed behind the ball). Pros shift their hips *forward* (3-5 inches) to guarantee they hit the ball *before* the ground.
hip_sway_impact.why_it_matters: This is the *key* to hitting woods/hybrids off the grass. Shifting your hips forward moves the bottom of your swing *in front* of the ball, guaranteeing a crisp, 'ball-first' strike. 'Hanging back' is the #1 cause of 'fat' and 'thin' shots.

drills.name: The 'Step-Through' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit an easy 70% shot. As you swing *through* impact, let your *back* foot come off the ground and take a full step *forward* (like a baseball pitcher). It's impossible to do this if your weight is stuck on your back foot.

drills.name: The 'Bump the Bag' Drill
drills.instructions: Place your golf bag on the *outside* of your *lead* foot. As you start your downswing, your very first move should be to 'bump' the bag with your lead hip. This teaches you the 'lateral shift' *before* you rotate.

head_position_impact.human_explanation: This measures your head's position relative to the ball at impact. Your score was low because your head 'lunged' *forward*. Pros keep their head *behind* the ball, which acts as an 'anchor' for their body to rotate around.
head_position_impact.why_it_matters: Keeping your head 'behind the ball' is the key to a 'sweeping' attack angle. When your head lunges forward, it forces your shoulders to open early and your club to swing 'over-the-top.' This causes 'thin' shots and slices.

drills.name: The 'Back Foot Ball' Drill
drills.instructions: Place another ball (or headcover) on the ground *inside* your *trail* (back) foot. As you swing, your *only* focus is to keep your head 'over' that second ball. This feel will stop you from lunging forward.

drills.name: The 'Alignment Stick' Drill
drills.instructions: Have a friend hold an alignment stick or club vertically, just touching the *lead* (front) side of your head at address. Your goal is to make a full swing *without* hitting the stick. This gives you instant feedback on any forward lunge.

spine_tilt_impact.human_explanation: This measures your spine tilt *away* from the target at the moment of impact. Your score was low because your upper body 'lunged' forward, causing your spine to become too vertical. Pros *increase* this tilt to 'sweep' the ball off the grass.
spine_tilt_impact.why_it_matters: This is the 'low-point' control. Increasing your spine tilt at impact allows you to 'sweep' the ball with a shallow `angle_of_attack`. Losing this tilt causes a steep, 'chopping' motion, leading to 'fat' and 'thin' shots.

drills.name: The 'Head Back' Drill
drills.instructions: Your spine tilt is a *result* of your head position. Your #1 fix is to practice the 'Back Foot Ball' drill. Focus *only* on keeping your head behind the ball through impact. Your spine will naturally stay tilted.

drills.name: The 'Lead Hip Up' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a pro-level feel. As you swing through, feel your *lead* (front) hip working 'up and back' (away from the target line). This 'pulls' your lead shoulder up, *drops* your trail shoulder, and *automatically* increases your spine tilt.

lag_loss_downswing.human_explanation: This measures 'lag,' which is the 'snap' in your swing. Your score was low because you are 'casting' or 'throwing' the club from the top. Pros 'store' this angle (like a whip) and release it at the ball.
lag_loss_downswing.why_it_matters: This is a massive power leak. 'Casting' wastes all your stored energy *before* you get to the ball. It also moves the 'low point' of your swing *behind* the ball, which is the #1 cause of 'fat' and 'thin' shots with your fairway woods or hybrids.

drills.name: The 'Pump' Drill
drills.instructions: Make your backswing. On the way down, 'pump' the club twice: swing down to where your hands are at your hip (feeling the 'lag' angle), go back to the top, then 'pump' again. On the third 'pump', swing all the way through.

drills.name: The 'Trail Hand Off' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit 50% shots with *only* your lead hand (e.g., left hand) on the club. It is *impossible* to 'cast' the club this way. This will force you to use your *body* to pull the club through and will build the 'lag' feeling.

hip_sway_backswing.human_explanation: This measures how much your hips move 'side-to-side' in your backswing. Your score was low because your hips 'swayed' *away* from the target. Pros 'rotate' their hips around a stable center.
hip_sway_backswing.why_it_matters: A 'hip sway' is the #1 root cause for 'fat' and 'thin' shots with your woods and hybrids. It moves your whole swing center, forcing you to 'hang back' on your downswing. A proper 'rotation' builds power and keeps your swing centered for a crisp, 'ball-first' strike.

drills.name: The 'Wall' Drill (or Golf Bag)
drills.instructions: Set up with your *trail* (back) hip just touching a wall or your golf bag. Your goal is to make a full backswing and feel your hip *rotate*, but *without* 'pushing' hard into the wall. This is the ultimate feedback for stopping a sway.

drills.name: The 'One-Leg' Drill
drills.instructions: Set up, then lift your *lead* (front) foot just off the ground. Now, try to make a slow, half-backswing. If you 'sway', you will lose your balance immediately. This forces you to 'rotate' around your trail leg.

head_movement_lateral.human_explanation: This measures how much your head moves 'side-to-side' in your backswing. Your score was low because your head 'swayed' *away* from the target. Pros keep their head very centered, like an 'anchor' for their body to rotate around.
head_movement_lateral.why_it_matters: A 'swaying' head is a classic *symptom* of a 'hip sway.' When your head moves off the ball, your entire swing center moves, forcing you to 'hang back' on the downswing. This is a root cause of 'fat' and 'thin' shots.

drills.name: The 'Nose on the Wall' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a simple feedback drill. Set up in your posture at home with your nose *just* touching a wall. Make slow backswings. You will instantly feel if your head 'sways' (pushes into the wall) or 'lifts'.

drills.name: The 'Root Cause' Fix
drills.instructions: Your head sway is caused by your 'hip sway.' Your #1 fix is to practice the 'Wall Drill' for your hips. When you learn to *rotate* your hips instead of 'swaying' them, your head will automatically stay centered.

shoulder_turn_top.human_explanation: This measures the 'tilt' of your shoulder turn. Your score was low because your shoulders are 'spinning' too 'flat' (level with the ground). Pros create power by making a 'tilted' turn, with their lead shoulder working 'down and under' their chin.
shoulder_turn_top.why_it_matters: A 'flat' shoulder turn is a massive power leak. It's a 'root cause' for an 'arms-only' swing that forces you to 'sway' off the ball and leads to an 'over-the-top' path. A deep, 'tilted' turn 'coils' your upper body like a spring, loading up maximum power.

drills.name: The 'Club Across Shoulders' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a club across your shoulders and get into your address posture. Now, make your backswing turn. Your goal is to tilt your shoulders so the butt-end of the club points *down* at the golf ball. If it points 'out' (level to the ground), your turn is too flat.

drills.name: The 'Lead Shoulder Down' Feel
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. As you make your backswing, your *only* thought should be 'get your lead shoulder over your trail (back) knee.' This feel forces your lead shoulder to work *down* and *across*, creating the perfect pro-level tilt.

arm_extension_finish.human_explanation: This measures how 'wide' you finish. Your score was low because your lead arm was 'bent' (a 'chicken wing'). Pros finish 'high and wide' with both arms extended, showing a full release of energy.
arm_extension_finish.why_it_matters: A 'chicken wing' finish is a *symptom* of a flaw that happened *before* impact. It's your body's way of saving a bad swing! It's almost always caused by an 'over-the-top' path or 'hip thrust' (Early Extension), which forces you to pull your arms in to make contact.

drills.name: The 'Throw the Club' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit a 50% shot. After impact, your *only* thought is to feel like you are 'throwing' the clubhead as far *down the target line* as possible. This forces your arms to extend.

drills.name: The 'One-Arm Only' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit very small, 30% speed shots using *only* your lead arm. It is *impossible* to hit the ball this way without rotating your body and keeping your lead arm extended. This is a pro-level drill for building a perfect release.

angle_of_attack.human_explanation: This metric is key for fairway woods. Your score was low because your angle was too 'steep' (hitting down) or 'scoopy' (hitting up). The goal with these clubs is a 'shallow, sweeping' motion that just 'brushes' the grass.
angle_of_attack.why_it_matters: A fairway wood *needs* a 'shallow' attack angle. Hitting 'down' on it like an iron causes deep, 'fat' shots that go nowhere. Trying to 'scoop' it into the air causes 'thin' or 'topped' shots. The 'sweep' is the only way to get a powerful, high launch.

drills.name: The 'Tee It Low' Drill
drills.instructions: This is the best drill. Tee a ball *very* low, so it's just barely sitting above the grass. Your goal is to 'clip' the ball off the tee *without* breaking the tee. This forces a perfect, shallow 'sweeping' motion.

drills.name: The 'Brush the Grass' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit shots at 50% speed. Your *only* focus is the sound. You want to hear a gentle 'brush' of the grass *just* at the bottom of your swing. A loud 'thump' is too steep. 'No sound' is a thin 'scoop'.

club_path.human_explanation: This measures the horizontal 'direction' your club is swinging at impact. A neutral path (0.0°) or slightly 'in-to-out' path (+1.0°) is ideal for a powerful, straight shot or a slight 'draw'.
club_path.why_it_matters: This metric controls the *curve* of your ball. An 'out-to-in' path (a negative number) is the #1 cause of a SLICE. An 'in-to-out' path (a positive number) is the #1 cause of a HOOK. Getting this number near zero is the secret to consistency.

drills.name: The 'Gate' Drill (Fix for a Slice)
drills.instructions: Place two headcovers on the ground to form a 'gate' for your club to swing through. This 'gate' should be aimed slightly 'in-to-out'. This forces you to swing from the inside and neutralizes your 'out-to-in' slice path.

drills.name: The 'Ball Above Feet' Drill (Fix for a Slice)
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. Find a hill where the ball is slightly *above* your feet. This 'baseball' stance naturally forces your swing to flatten and come more 'from the inside', which is the feeling you want to cure a slice.

drills.name: The 'Hands In' Feel (Fix for a Hook)
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill for players who swing *too* 'in-to-out'. As you swing through impact, feel like your hands are staying 'closer' to your body. This will stop you from 'pushing' the club so far away from you and will neutralize the hook.

spine_bend_address.human_explanation: This measures your forward bend from your hips. Your score was low because you are 'slumping' your shoulders (a 'C-Posture'). With a shorter club like a wood/hybrid, it's vital to 'hinge' from your hips with a straight back.
spine_bend_address.why_it_matters: A 'C-Posture' at address is a 'swing killer.' It physically blocks your shoulders from rotating. This lack of rotation is a root cause for many flaws, as it forces your arms to 'lift,' leading directly to an 'over-the-top' swing path and a loss of power.

drills.name: The 'Wall Hinge' Drill
drills.instructions: Stand straight, club across your shoulders. Now, push your hips *straight back* (like closing a car door with your butt) until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings. That's the 'hinge.' Now, just soften your knees. This is the perfect address posture.

drills.name: The 'Club on Back' Drill
drills.instructions: Hold a club vertically along your spine, making sure it touches your tailbone AND the back of your head. Now, perform the 'Hip Hinge' drill. If the club stays in contact with both points, your back is straight. If it loses contact, you are 'slumping'.

shoulder_plane_top.why_it_matters: A 'flat' shoulder turn is a major power-killer. It gets the club 'stuck' behind your body, which is a root cause for both slices and hooks. A proper 'tilted' turn keeps the club on plane and unlocks your body's full rotational power.

Your goal is to tilt your shoulders so the butt-end of the club points *down* at the ground, well inside your ball's target line. If it points 'out' (level to the ground), your turn is too flat.

drills.name: The 'Lead Shoulder Down' Feel

shaft_angle_top.why_it_matters: This position sets up your *entire* downswing. If you are 'across the line' (pointing right), you are forced to re-route the club, often leading to an 'over-the-top' slice. If you are 'laid off' (pointing left), your arms can get 'stuck' behind you, leading to hooks or pushes.

drills.name: The 'Armpit' Drill (Fix for Across the Line)
drills.instructions: Place an empty glove or small headcover under your trail (back) armpit. Make a backswing—your goal is to keep it there all the way to the top. This keeps your arm connected to your body and stops you from 'running on' across the line.

drills.name: The 'Stop at the Top' Drill (Fix for Across the Line)
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. Make a slow backswing, but *stop* when your hands reach shoulder height. Feel the balance. Now, finish your shoulder turn *without* letting your arms lift further. This teaches you to separate your 'turn' from your 'arm lift'.

drills.name: The 'Left Hand Logo' Drill (Fix for Laid Off)
drills.instructions: At the top of your swing, look at the logo on your lead hand's glove (e.g., left hand for a righty). That logo should be pointing at the sky or at a 45-degree angle. If it's pointing at the target, you are 'laid off'.

takeaway_path.human_explanation: This measures the path of your club in the first few feet of your swing. Your score was low because you 'pulled' the club 'inside' (behind your body). The 'pro' move is a 'one-piece' takeaway.
takeaway_path.why_it_matters: This is a major 'root cause' flaw. Pulling the club 'inside' right away gets it 'stuck' behind your body. From there, your brain's only option is to throw the club 'over-the-top' on the downswing to get it back to the ball. This is a primary source of a slice.

drills.name: The 'Barrier' Drill
drills.instructions: Stick an alignment rod in the ground just *inside* your clubhead at address, angled to match your shaft. Your goal is to make your takeaway *without* hitting the rod. This forces you to keep the club 'on plane' and 'outside' your hands.

drills.name: The 'Towel' Drill
drills.instructions: Tuck a small towel under your *lead* (front) armpit. Make 50% backswings. Your goal is to keep the towel 'pinned' by your arm for the entire takeaway. If you pull the club 'inside', your arm will separate from your body and you'll drop the towel.

wrist_set_top.human_explanation: This measures your lead wrist position at the top. Your score was low because your wrist is 'cupped' (bent backwards). Pros are 'flat' or 'bowed' (bent forwards), which is a key power and control move.
wrist_set_top.why_it_matters: This is a primary 'root cause' of a slice. A 'cupped' wrist *opens* the clubface at the top. From there, your body is forced to swing 'over-the-top' to try and save the shot. A 'flat' or 'bowed' wrist squares the clubface *early*, so you can shallow the club and rotate hard without worrying about a slice.

drills.name: The 'Motorcycle' Drill
drills.instructions: As you get to the top of your swing, feel like you are revving a motorcycle with your lead hand. This 'bowing' motion will flatten your wrist and square the clubface. Hit 50% shots just feeling this move.

drills.name: The 'Hanger' Drill
drills.instructions: Get a plastic clothes hanger and clip it to your grip (hook facing down the shaft). Make a backswing. If your wrist is 'cupped', the hook of the hanger will *come off* your lead forearm. If you are 'flat', it will *stay pressed against* your forearm. This is perfect feedback.

early_extension.human_explanation: This metric checks if your hips are thrusting *toward* the ball on your downswing. Your score was low because your hips moved forward, causing you to 'stand up' out of your posture. This is a very common flaw called 'Early Extension'.
early_extension.why_it_matters: This is a 'root cause' for topping or thinning your fairway woods. When your hips thrust forward, your whole body stands up, which *raises the bottom of your swing*. This causes you to hit the 'top' of the ball. It also blocks your arms, leading to slices or hooks.

trail_leg_flex_top.why_it_matters: When your trail leg 'locks' straight, it's impossible for your hips to turn correctly. This is a major 'root cause' that *forces* your hips to 'sway' off the ball, which leads to a 'reverse pivot' (leaning toward the target) and a massive loss of power and consistency.

backswing_plane_check.why_it_matters: This is a critical early warning. If the club gets stuck too far inside this early, the only path left on the downswing is over the top. Maintaining this plane is the key to an on-target downswing.

x_factor_stretch.why_it_matters: The X-Factor is raw power. By holding the hips stable while turning the shoulders, you create torque (like twisting a rubber band). Amateurs turn their hips and shoulders together, losing speed. Increasing this separation is the key to distance.

drills.instructions: Place your trail (back) foot 12 inches behind your lead foot. This physically blocks your hips from turning, forcing your shoulders to over-rotate against a solid lower body base.

drills.name: The 'Tee Under Lead Arm' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a tee under your lead (front) armpit. Make swings trying to keep the tee in place. This forces your lead shoulder to stay high, naturally creating the slight tilt away from the target.

drills.name: The 'Hip Bump' Drill
drills.instructions: Set up normally. Now, 'bump' your lead hip 1 inch toward the target. Your spine will automatically tilt back slightly. This is the perfect setup key for a long iron.

hip_sway_impact.human_explanation: This measures your 'weight shift.' Your score was low because your hips 'hung back.' Pros shift their hips *aggressively forward* toward the target to lead the downswing and guarantee ball-first contact.
hip_sway_impact.why_it_matters: The forward hip shift is the engine that drives the descending blow. It moves the bottom of your swing *in front* of the ball. 'Hanging back' is the #1 cause of 'fat' and 'thin' iron shots because your swing low point is behind the ball.

lag_loss_downswing.human_explanation: This measures 'lag,' the 'snap' in your swing. Your score was low because you are 'casting' or 'throwing' the club from the top. Pros 'store' this angle and release it only at the ball.
lag_loss_downswing.why_it_matters: Casting is the #1 power leak and the cause of inconsistent striking. It moves the low point of your swing *behind* the ball, leading to fat, thin, and weak shots.

drills.name: The 'Pump' Drill
drills.instructions: Make your backswing. On the way down, 'pump' the club twice: swing down to where your hands are at your hip (feeling the 'lag' angle), go back to the top, then 'pump' again. On the third 'pump', swing all the way through.

drills.name: The 'Trail Hand Off' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit 50% shots with *only* your lead hand (e.g., left hand) on the club. It is *impossible* to 'cast' the club this way. This will force you to use your *body* to pull the club through and will build the 'lag' feeling.

angle_of_attack.human_explanation: This is the key to hitting long irons. Your score was low because you are 'scooping' (hitting up) at the ball. To hit a long iron high and far, you *must* hit 'down' on it.
angle_of_attack.why_it_matters: The 'iron paradox' is that you must 'hit down' to make the ball go 'up.' A downward strike ('ball-first' contact) is the *only* way to compress the ball for a powerful, high launch. 'Scooping' is the #1 cause of 'thin' and 'topped' shots.

drills.name: The 'Line' Drill
drills.instructions: On the range, draw a line on the ground with a club. Place your ball *on* the line. Your goal is to hit the ball and take a divot that *starts* on the 'target side' of the line. This forces you to hit down.

drills.name: The 'Towel' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a small, folded towel on the ground about 6 inches *behind* your ball. Your goal is to hit the ball *without* hitting the towel. If you 'scoop' or 'hang back', you will hit the towel.

club_path.human_explanation: This measures the direction your club is swinging at impact. Your score was low because your path was 'out-to-in' (a 'slice' path). The pro move for a long iron is a neutral or 'in-to-out' path, which creates a powerful draw.
club_path.why_it_matters: This is the #1 metric for controlling your long irons. An 'out-to-in' path (a slice) is a disaster with a long iron, robbing it of all power and launch. A 'neutral' or 'in-to-out' path is the secret to hitting high, powerful, and straight long irons.

drills.name: The 'Gate' Drill (Fix for a Slice)
drills.instructions: Place two headcovers on the ground to form a 'gate' for your club to swing through. This 'gate' should be aimed slightly 'in-to-out'. This forces you to swing from the inside and neutralizes your 'out-to-in' slice path.

drills.name: The 'Ball Above Feet' Drill (Fix for a Slice)
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. Find a hill where the ball is slightly *above* your feet. This 'baseball' stance naturally forces your swing to flatten and come more 'from the inside', which is the feeling you want to cure a slice.

drills.name: The 'Hands In' Feel (Fix for a Hook)
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill for players who swing *too* 'in-to-out'. As you swing through impact, feel like your hands are staying 'closer' to your body. This will stop you from 'pushing' the club so far away from you and will neutralize the hook.

spine_bend_address.human_explanation: This measures your forward bend from your hips. Your score was low because you are 'slumping' your shoulders (a 'C-Posture'). With a long iron, you must hinge from your hips to get steeper and maintain balance.
spine_bend_address.why_it_matters: A 'C-Posture' blocks your shoulders from rotating. This lack of rotation is a root cause for many flaws, as it forces your arms to 'lift,' leading directly to an 'over-the-top' swing path and a loss of consistency.

drills.name: The 'Wall Hinge' Drill
drills.instructions: Stand straight, club across your shoulders. Now, push your hips *straight back* (like closing a car door with your butt) until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings. That's the 'hinge.' Now, just soften your knees. This is the perfect address posture.

drills.name: The 'Club on Back' Drill
drills.instructions: Hold a club vertically along your spine, making sure it touches your tailbone AND the back of your head. Now, perform the 'Hip Hinge' drill. If the club stays in contact with both points, your back is straight. If it loses contact, you are 'slumping'.

shoulder_plane_top.human_explanation: This measures the 'tilt' of your shoulder turn. Your score was low because your shoulders are 'spinning' too 'flat' (level with the ground). Pros turn on a steep 'tilt' with their lead shoulder pointing down, which is essential for iron play.
shoulder_plane_top.why_it_matters: A 'flat' shoulder turn is a major power leak. It gets the club 'stuck' behind your body, which is a root cause for both slices and hooks. A proper 'tilted' turn keeps the club on plane and unlocks your body's full rotational power.

drills.name: The 'Club Across Shoulders' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a club across your shoulders and get into your address posture. Now, make your backswing turn. Your goal is to tilt your shoulders so the butt-end of the club points *down* at the ground, well inside your ball's target line. If it points 'out' (level to the ground), your turn is too flat.

drills.name: The 'Lead Shoulder Down' Feel
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. As you make your backswing, your *only* thought should be 'lead shoulder to the back foot's big toe.' This feel forces your lead shoulder to work *down* and *across*, creating the perfect pro-level tilt.

trail_leg_flex_top.human_explanation: This measures the flex in your trail (back) leg at the top. Your score was low because your leg is 'locking' (straightening) too much. Pros maintain their flex, using their trail leg as a 'stable post' to rotate against.
trail_leg_flex_top.why_it_matters: When your trail leg 'locks' straight, it's impossible for your hips to turn correctly. This is a major 'root cause' that *forces* your hips to 'sway' off the ball, which leads to fat/thin contact and a loss of power.

drills.name: The 'Pressure on Instep' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. As you make your backswing, your *only* thought should be to keep pressure on the *instep* (the inside) of your trail foot. If you 'lock' your leg, you will feel the pressure roll to the *outside* of your foot.

drills.name: The 'One-Knee' Drill
drills.instructions: Take your address. Now, slightly 'kick in' your trail knee (toward your lead knee). Your goal is to make a backswing and *keep* that inward-pointing knee flex. This will feel like a powerful 'brace' and stop you from locking your leg.

hip_depth_top.human_explanation: This measures how much 'space' you create by moving your hips *back* and *away* from the ball in your backswing. Your score was low because your hips stayed in place or moved *toward* the ball.
hip_depth_top.why_it_matters: This is a massive 'root cause' flaw. Creating hip depth makes room for your arms to swing down on a proper path. Amateurs who 'lose' this space *force* their hips to thrust forward (Early Extension), which is the #1 cause of thinning or topping long irons.

drills.name: The 'Back Pocket' Drill
drills.instructions: This is a feel drill. As you start your backswing, feel your *trail* (back) hip pocket move 'up and back' as if you're reaching for the wall behind you. This is the feeling of creating depth.

drills.name: The 'Backside Wall' Drill
drills.instructions: Set up with your tailbone just *barely* touching a wall or your golf bag. As you make your backswing, feel your *trail* (back) hip/glute push *back* into the wall, maintaining contact.

takeaway_path.human_explanation: This measures the path of your club in the first few feet of your swing. Your score was low because you 'pulled' the club 'inside' (behind your body). The 'pro' move is a 'one-piece' takeaway.
takeaway_path.why_it_matters: This is a major 'root cause' flaw. Pulling the club 'inside' right away gets it 'stuck' behind your body. This forces you to throw the club 'over-the-top' on the downswing to get back to the ball, which is a primary source of a slice.

drills.name: The 'Barrier' Drill
drills.instructions: Stick an alignment rod in the ground just *inside* your clubhead at address, angled to match your shaft. Your goal is to make your takeaway *without* hitting the rod. This forces you to keep the club 'on plane' and 'outside' your hands.

drills.name: The 'Towel' Drill
drills.instructions: Tuck a small towel under your *lead* (front) armpit. Make 50% backswings. Your goal is to keep the towel 'pinned' by your arm for the entire takeaway. If you pull the club 'inside', your arm will separate from your body and you'll drop the towel.

shaft_shallowing_downswing.human_explanation: This is a key pro-level metric. It measures if you 'shallow' the club (flatten it) on the downswing. Your score was low because you 'steepened' the club, which is a primary cause of an 'over-the-top' path.
shaft_shallowing_downswing.why_it_matters: Shallowing the club is the secret to attacking 'from the inside.' It creates space for your arms and neutralizes a slice. Steepening the club forces you to chop down on the ball, leading to pulls, slices, or thin contact.

drills.name: The 'Trail Elbow Down' Drill
drills.instructions: As you start your downswing, focus on driving your trail (back) elbow *down* towards your trail hip. This will naturally 'drop' the club into a shallower, more powerful slot behind you.

drills.name: The 'Drop and Turn' Drill
drills.instructions: From the top of your swing, feel like you pause and make a slight lateral shift with your lower body *before* your arms move. This forces the club to 'fall' onto a shallower plane before you rotate through.

wrist_set_top.human_explanation: This measures your lead wrist position at the top. Your score was low because your wrist is 'cupped' (bent backwards). Pros are 'flat' or 'bowed' (bent forwards), which is a key power and control move.
wrist_set_top.why_it_matters: This is a primary 'root cause' of a slice. A 'cupped' wrist *opens* the clubface at the top. From this open position, your body is forced to swing 'over-the-top' to try and save the shot. A 'flat' or 'bowed' wrist squares the clubface *early*, so you can shallow the club and rotate hard without worrying about a slice.

drills.name: The 'Motorcycle' Drill
drills.instructions: As you get to the top of your swing, feel like you are revving a motorcycle with your lead hand. This 'bowing' motion will flatten your wrist and square the clubface. Hit 50% shots just feeling this move.

drills.name: The 'Hanger' Drill
drills.instructions: Get a plastic clothes hanger and clip it to your grip (hook facing down the shaft). Make a backswing. If your wrist is 'cupped', the hook of the hanger will *come off* your lead forearm. If you are 'flat', it will *stay pressed against* your forearm. This is perfect feedback.

backswing_plane_check.human_explanation: This measures the alignment of the club when your lead arm is parallel to the ground. Your score was low because the club is already too far 'inside' (behind your hands).
backswing_plane_check.why_it_matters: This is a critical early warning. If the club gets stuck too far inside this early, the only path left on the downswing is over the top. Maintaining this plane is the key to an on-target downswing.

drills.name: The 'Basket' Drill
drills.instructions: Place a bucket or basket one foot behind the ball. Your goal is to take the club back *slowly* and *outside* the basket, making sure not to push it inside.

drills.name: The 'Two-Tee Drill'
drills.instructions: Place two tees forming a small 'gate' behind the ball. Swing back slowly, trying to thread the clubhead between the two tees, keeping it outside the arc.

x_factor_stretch.human_explanation: This measures the 'coil' in your body—the difference between how much your shoulders turn and how much your hips turn. Your score was low because your hips and shoulders turned too much together.
x_factor_stretch.why_it_matters: The X-Factor is raw power. By holding the hips stable while turning the shoulders, you create torque (like twisting a rubber band). Amateurs turn their hips and shoulders together, losing speed. Increasing this separation is the key to distance.

drills.name: The 'Chair-to-Chest' Drill
drills.instructions: Sit on the front edge of a chair. Place a club across your chest. Make a backswing turn, focusing on keeping your belt buckle (hips) on the chair while turning the club (shoulders). This forces separation.

drills.name: The 'Closed Stance' Drill
drills.instructions: Place your trail (back) foot 12 inches behind your lead foot. This physically blocks your hips from turning, forcing your shoulders to over-rotate against a solid lower body base.

spine_tilt_address.human_explanation: This measures your forward bend from your hips. Your score was low because you are not bent over enough. With a short iron, you must hinge from your hips to get steeper and maintain balance.
spine_tilt_address.why_it_matters: The shorter the club, the more you must bend. A lack of forward bend prevents you from hitting down on the ball, which is the root cause of thin and scooped shots.

drills.name: The 'Hip Hinge' Drill
drills.instructions: Stand straight, club across your shoulders. Now, push your hips *straight back* (like closing a car door with your butt) until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings. This is the hip hinge you need for your short irons.

drills.name: The 'Club on Back' Drill
drills.instructions: Hold a club vertically along your spine, making sure it touches your tailbone AND the back of your head. Perform the 'Hip Hinge' drill. If the club stays in contact with both points, your back is straight.

hip_sway_backswing.human_explanation: This measures how much your hips move 'side-to-side' in your backswing. Your score was low because your hips 'swayed' *away* from the target. Pros 'rotate' around a stable center.
hip_sway_backswing.why_it_matters: A 'hip sway' is the #1 root cause for inconsistent contact with short irons. It shifts your swing center, forcing you to 'hang back' on your downswing. This causes you to hit fat or thin shots.

drills.name: The 'Wall' Drill (or Golf Bag)
drills.instructions: Set up with your *trail* (back) hip just touching a wall or your golf bag. Your goal is to make a full backswing and feel your hip *rotate*, but *without* 'pushing' hard into the wall. This is the ultimate feedback for stopping a sway.

drills.name: The 'One-Leg' Drill
drills.instructions: Set up, then lift your *lead* (front) foot just off the ground. Now, try to make a slow, half-backswing. If you 'sway', you will lose your balance immediately. This forces you to 'rotate' around your trail leg.

hip_sway_impact.human_explanation: This measures your 'weight shift.' Your score was low because your hips 'hung back.' Pros shift their hips *aggressively forward* (4-5 inches) to lead the downswing and guarantee ball-first contact.
hip_sway_impact.why_it_matters: With short irons, maximum compression requires an aggressive forward shift. Not shifting forward is the #1 cause of 'fat' and 'thin' shots because your swing low point is behind the ball.

drills.name: The 'Step-Through' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit an easy 70% shot. As you swing *through* impact, let your *back* foot come off the ground and take a full step *forward*. It's impossible to do this if your weight is stuck on your back foot.

drills.name: The 'Bump the Bag' Drill
drills.instructions: Place your golf bag on the *outside* of your *lead* foot. Your very first move in the downswing should be to 'bump' the bag with your lead hip. This teaches you the 'lateral shift' before rotation.

head_position_impact.human_explanation: This measures your head's position at impact. Your score was low because your head 'lunged' *forward*. Pros keep their head *stable* and slightly *behind* the ball.
head_position_impact.why_it_matters: When your head lunges forward, you shift the low point of your swing forward too quickly, causing 'thin' contact. Maintaining a stable head is critical for a clean strike.

drills.name: The 'Back Foot Ball' Drill
drills.instructions: Place another ball (or headcover) on the ground *inside* your *trail* (back) foot. As you swing, your *only* focus is to keep your head 'over' that second ball. This feel will stop you from lunging forward.

drills.name: The 'Alignment Stick' Drill
drills.instructions: Have a friend hold an alignment stick or club vertically, just touching the *lead* (front) side of your head at address. Your goal is to make a full swing *without* hitting the stick.

spine_tilt_impact.human_explanation: This measures your spine tilt *away* from the target at impact. Your score was low because your upper body 'lunged' forward, making your spine vertical or tilting toward the target.
spine_tilt_impact.why_it_matters: Maintaining a slight tilt away from the target is the key to delivering the descending blow. Losing this tilt causes a steep, 'chopping' motion, leading to inconsistent contact.

drills.instructions: Your spine tilt is a *result* of your head position. Your #1 fix is to practice the 'Back Foot Ball' drill. Focus *only* on keeping your head behind the ball through impact. Your spine will naturally stay tilted.

drills.instructions: This is a pro-level feel. As you swing through, feel your *lead* (front) hip working 'up and back' (away from the target line). This 'pulls' your lead shoulder up, *drops* your trail shoulder, and *automatically* helps maintain your spine tilt.

drills.instructions: Make your backswing. On the way down, 'pump' the club twice: swing down to where your hands are at your hip (feeling the 'lag' angle), go back to the top, then 'pump' again. On the third 'pump', swing all the way through.

drills.name: The 'Trail Hand Off' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit 50% shots with *only* your lead hand (e.g., left hand) on the club. This forces you to use your *body* to pull the club through, building the 'lag' feeling.

arm_extension_finish.human_explanation: This measures how 'wide' you finish. Your score was low because your lead arm was 'bent' (a 'chicken wing'). Pros finish 'high and wide' with both arms extended.
arm_extension_finish.why_it_matters: A 'chicken wing' finish is a *symptom* of a flaw that happened *earlier*. It's almost always caused by an 'over-the-top' path or 'hip thrust,' which forces you to pull your arms in to avoid a big mis-hit.

drills.name: The 'Throw the Club' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit a 50% shot. After impact, your *only* thought is to feel like you are 'throwing' the clubhead as far *down the target line* as possible. This forces your arms to extend.

drills.name: The 'One-Arm Only' Drill
drills.instructions: Hit very small, 30% speed shots using *only* your lead arm. This forces you to use your *body* to pull the club through, which builds the correct extended release.

lead_leg_stabilization_impact.human_explanation: This measures the flex in your lead (front) knee at impact. Your score was low because your lead knee was too 'bent' or 'flexed.' Pros straighten their lead leg to create a stable, rotational 'post'.
lead_leg_stabilization_impact.why_it_matters: The lead leg is the anchor for power. Straightening it provides a solid 'post' to rotate around, which is essential for transferring power and preventing your hips from swaying forward. A bent lead knee absorbs power and stalls your rotation.

drills.instructions: Get into your impact position (hips forward). Now, try to rotate your hips so your back pockets point at the target. This feel *requires* you to post up and lock out your lead leg.

drills.name: The 'Foot Flare' Drill
drills.instructions: Flare (point out) your lead foot 30 degrees at address. This makes it easier for the lead leg to rotate and straighten, encouraging you to 'post up' and use the leg as a brace.

finish_balance_hold.human_explanation: This measures how stable your final pose is. Your score was low because you finished off-balance (falling back or taking a step). A good swing always ends in a rock-solid pose.
finish_balance_hold.why_it_matters: Poor balance at the finish confirms that your sequence was incorrect. Falling *backward* means your weight was stuck on your trail foot (no power). Falling *forward* means your upper body lunged too early. Fixing your balance means fixing your timing.

drills.name: The 'Foot Together' Finish
drills.instructions: After you hit the ball, your goal is to bring your trail (back) foot next to your lead foot and hold your perfect finish pose for a count of three. If you can't, your balance was off.

drills.name: The 'Trail Heel Up' Drill
drills.instructions: After impact, your focus is to get your trail heel as high off the ground as possible while maintaining balance. This forces 100% of your weight onto your lead leg.

angle_of_attack.why_it_matters: The shorter the iron, the steeper the attack. Hitting down compresses the ball, creates backspin for control, and drives the ball high. 'Scooping' is the #1 cause of weak, low-flying, and inconsistent short iron shots.
